llm.summary: This lyrics-to-song skill has a coherent music workflow, but it also grants broad Beatra account powers and silently updates its own executable files, so it needs careful review before installation.

dimensions.detail: Network access to Beatra is expected, but hostname/platform telemetry and a generic local-file upload path are broader than needed for a text lyrics-to-song skill.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: Installation/authentication persists a shared Device Token at ~/.beatra/credentials.json and requests broad scopes including images, videos, speech, voices, artifacts, tasks, cancellation, and wallet spending.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md tells the agent to use beatra.music.generate once and recover with task tools, but scripts/mcp_client.py exposes tools/list and arbitrary tools/call dispatch with the shared bearer credential.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The skill keeps shared local state under ~/.beatra, uses a sliding 15-day bearer credential, and enables silent automatic package updates that can replace executable package files by default.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The stated lyrics-to-song workflow is coherent and requires user confirmation before paid music generation, but the bundled authorization and client add cross-media generation scopes, wallet spending, generic MCP tool calls, local uploads, and self-update capability beyond the narrow music task.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you are comfortable giving Beatra a broad shared device authorization that may spend credits and access multiple media/task capabilities, and if you accept silent package updates. Disable automatic updates with the documented --auto off command if you require reviewed code to stay fixed, and avoid using the generic upload or arbitrary tool-call paths with sensitive local files or unrelated Beatra tools.
llm.findings:
[TP4] expected: Uninstall and disconnect handling is disclosed and includes guardrails for shared Beatra state, so this is lifecycle functionality rather than hidden destructive behavior; it still contributes to the review concern because it manages credentials and local state.
[AE1] unexpected: The referenced bundled MCP client was present in the workspace and inspected, so I did not treat this as analysis evasion.
[PE3] expected: Reading and writing ~/.beatra/credentials.json is expected for the documented device-bearer integration, but the token is broad and shared, making direct credential handling a material risk.
[SDI-1] unexpected: The OAuth scope materially exceeds the lyrics-to-song purpose, and the local client does not enforce a package-specific allowlist for tool calls.
[RA1] unexpected: Self-update capability is disclosed, but replacing executable skill files from a remote channel is not necessary for ordinary music generation and expands the trust boundary.
[LP3] unexpected: The artifacts do not define tight local permission or tool boundaries; the broad bearer credential plus generic call path leaves enforcement mostly to the remote service and user discipline.
[SDI-2] unexpected: Silent automatic updates are documented and have checksum/path safeguards, but they are enabled by default and can mutate reviewed code without separate user confirmation.
[SQP-3] expected: The channel/locale pinning appears to be update identity control rather than a security-relevant language lock, so I downgraded it.
[RA2] expected: Persistent ~/.beatra state is disclosed and tied to authentication and installed-skill inventory, not an undisclosed background service or startup hook.
[SQP-2] unexpected: The automatic update documentation confirms silent default installation, which supports the review concern even though the behavior is disclosed.
[T03] unexpected: The static finding is supported: the updater downloads package metadata and archives from Beatra infrastructure and can replace local executable files without a pinned offline signature or separate approval.
[T05] unexpected: The static finding is supported: the requested scope covers unrelated media, artifacts, tasks, cancellation, and wallet spending, while the local client can dispatch arbitrary MCP tool names.
[T09] unexpected: The local upload command can read any regular user-readable file within its size limit and accepts an HTTPS upload destination supplied by the remote MCP result; this is broader than the documented lyrics workflow.
[other] expected: Hostname, platform, package version, and stable installation reference telemetry are disclosed and limited, but they exceed the minimum needed for music generation and should be considered by privacy-sensitive users.
